I’ve been having a really hard time since that car accident a little while ago. I’m still going into the office a few days a week and working from home the rest, but I feel like I’m running on empty all the time. I technically sleep 7–8 hours most nights, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all. It’s like my body rests but my brain doesn’t. By mid-afternoon my eyes burn at the screen, and I’m rereading the same lines of code over and over.

What’s freaking me out the most are these moments where it feels like I’m back on the highway. It’s not just remembering it—I’ll hear brakes outside or see a sudden movement in my peripheral vision, and for a few seconds it’s like I’m right there again, waiting for the impact. My heart jumps, I lose track of what I’m doing, and then I sort of “snap” back to my desk or my apartment.

This has been going on for a bit now. I’m still doing my job, but slower, and I’m avoiding driving whenever I can. I feel worn down and not like myself.
D019-D020_h001.question_a:
About two weeks ago I was driving home from work when a truck ran a red light and slammed into the side of my car. I didn’t lose consciousness, but it was bad enough that the airbags went off and they took me to the ER. Physically I’m mostly okay now, just some lingering soreness, but my head hasn’t been right since.

I’m sleeping roughly 7–8 hours a night, but I wake up feeling like I barely slept at all—heavy, foggy, like I’ve pulled an all‑nighter debugging code. No matter how early I go to bed, I don’t feel rested the next day and it’s making it really hard to focus at work.

The worst part is these “reliving” moments. Sometimes when I hear a horn or see headlights in my peripheral vision, I’m suddenly back in the crash. For a few seconds I honestly feel like it’s happening again—the sound of metal, the airbag, the smell—it’s all there, and I kind of lose track of where I actually am. This has been going on consistently since about the third day after the accident and hasn’t let up.
D019-D020_h001.question_b:
About two months ago my apartment building caught fire. I wasn’t hurt, but I watched the smoke fill the hallway and really thought I might not make it out. For the first week or so after, I was jumpy and wired, which I figured was normal. But the stuff that’s bothering me now really kicked in maybe two weeks after the fire.

I sleep 7–8 hours, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t rested at all, like my body never really “shuts down.” I’m dragging through my workday, making stupid mistakes in code I’d usually catch easily, and I can’t focus in meetings.

Sometimes something small sets me off—a burning smell from someone’s toast, or a loud alarm at the office—and for a few seconds it’s like I’m back in that hallway. I’m not completely gone or losing blocks of time, but I get this brief, almost movie-like replay where my chest tightens and I feel like I’m there again.

This has been going on steadily for about six weeks now, and it hasn’t gotten bad enough to stop me from functioning, but it’s wearing me down.

I wake up with my heart racing and it’s hard to settle back down.

It’s been going on for a couple of months now, definitely more than a few days but not right away after the crash. I’m still going to work and doing the books, but I’m slower, more distracted, and exhausted. My husband says I’m more irritable and withdrawn.
